description: RESOLVED: controlled A/B test confirming operation_token is the real mechanism behind the E-21291-01718 ~2-minute lockout. Echoing back the previous PUT response's operation_token on the next write avoids the lockout entirely, even seconds apart.

sequence.step: A) baseline write, no token (establishes a fresh token)

rest of fixed fields, ai_control off etc

sequence.step: B) ~20s later, WITH operation_token from A
C) ~15s later, WITH operation_token from B
D) negative control, ~15s later, WITHOUT any operation_token

rest of fixed fields unchanged, no operation_token key at all

error.message: 他の機器でエアコンが制御されました。2分間変更できません。

notes: Clean 2-for-2 / 1-for-1 A/B result: WITH the previous response's token echoed back, both close-interval writes (B, C) succeeded at ~15-20s gaps that have repeatedly failed before. WITHOUT it (D), the very next write at the same ~15s interval failed identically to every prior occurrence.

This resolves the open question from captures 02/04/37: the lockout is NOT really about 'another device' (though a genuine second client, like the AVD app active during the earlier CLI session, could ALSO independently hold/invalidate the token) -- it's about write continuity via operation_token. Any write that doesn't echo the immediately-prior response's token looks like a competing/uncoordinated write and gets locked out, regardless of whether it's really from a different client or the same one just not tracking the token.

Implemented in coordinator.py: a new _operation_token_cache (dict[appliance_id, str], same pattern as silence_control/humidity caches, since operation_token has no GET readback -- confirmed across dozens of GET captures this session, only ever present on PUT responses) is now populated from every successful /status or /customsettings PUT response and echoed back as the operation_token field on the NEXT write to either endpoint. Shared between both endpoints since both are scoped to the same physical appliance; not separately confirmed whether their tokens are truly interchangeable, but no evidence yet that they aren't.

This was tested purely via the CLI against real hardware -- not yet re-verified through the actual HA integration with the new coordinator.py caching in place. Next step: redeploy and watch HA's debug logs for a rapid sequence of entity changes (e.g. adjusting fan speed then swing quickly) to confirm no more E-21291-01718 hits in normal usage.
